# Action reference

<!-- generated by scripts/gen-docs.ts, do not edit by hand (just docs-gen) -->

Every action is a chat command (`!name args`), an LLM tool and a typed call (`agent.act(name, params)`).
Positional chat arguments follow the parameter order below; `key=value` works too.

30 skills, 139 actions.

## base_projects

Long-term base projects: improving and extending the fortress by itself.

### `projects`

List the base projects (fortress walls, stone floor, lighting, storage chests, workshop, walkway, towers, a farm plot) in working order: what is done, ready, waiting for an owner's ok, skipped or blocked, the policy and what comes next. Answers "pax projects".

*non-exclusive*

No parameters.

### `project`

Owners: decide about a base project. approve (ok to build), veto (never), skip (not now), unskip, next (build it next, implies ok), pause / resume (all base work), reset (forget what was said about one, or all). Names: walls, floor, walkway, towers, lighting, storage, workshop, farm_plot.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `approve` \| `veto` \| `skip` \| `unskip` \| `next` \| `pause` \| `resume` \| `reset` | yes |  | approve | veto | skip | unskip | next | pause | resume | reset |
| `name` | string |  |  | the project (not for pause/resume); words like "chests" or "the towers" work |

### `plan_base`

Dry run of the base projects: finds the base (fits the fortress blueprint to what is built), surveys every project (blocks done and left, spots left alone because they hold someone else's blocks), the materials each still needs against what it carries and what its chests hold, where new things would go, and what it would do next. Builds nothing. Answers "pax plan fortress".

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detail` | boolean |  | `true` | add the materials and notes per project |

### `work_on_base`

One work session on the base projects (at most `minutes`): the next one in the queue, or the one named. Takes materials from its chests, gathers what is still missing (bounded), then builds only what is not there yet; never digs blocks it did not place itself except natural ones. Resumes where the last session stopped. Big projects need an owner's ok first (policy).

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string |  |  | work on this one (it must be ready, or an owner asks); default the next in the queue |
| `minutes` | number (1..60) |  |  | session length (default settings projects.sessionMinutes, 10) |

### `check_base`

Check the base for ways in for mobs: caves and holes under the floor, tunnels under the walls, a mine entrance next to the walls, dark spots mobs spawn on. Says what it found and how it would fix each (cap, fill, seal, light). Changes nothing. Answers "pax is the base safe".

*non-exclusive*

No parameters.

### `secure_base`

Make the base mob-proof now: cap a mine entrance by the walls, seal holes and tunnels into the base, fill small cavities under it, light what stays open (settings baseSafety). One bounded session; the base project "integrity" does the same between chores.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minutes` | number (1..30) |  | `5` | session length |

### `blueprint_design`

Check and save a blueprint you designed, as YAML (or JSON) in the blueprint format (see blueprint_show small_house for an example): name, description, facing (entrance side), roles {name: {default: block, accept?: regex, kind?: block|door|attachment|furnish, optional?}}, palette {char: role | "role[facing=north]" | {block: oak_stairs, state: {...}}}, layers bottom to top, each a list of rows north to south, columns west to east; " " = don't care, "." = air, ^ v < > = stairs of the roof role. It is validated (format, size, real block names, every block placeable in order, nothing floating); problems come back so you can fix and call again. Data only, nothing runs.

*non-exclusive*

| `save` | boolean |  | `true` | false: only check and preview |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | `false` | replace a learned blueprint of the same name |

## bodyguard

Protecting a player: stay with them, fight what threatens them, block arrows, feed them.

### `protect`

Stay with a player as a bodyguard until stopped: keep close (between them and the nearest danger), kill mobs that threaten them (creepers near them first, archers with a shot at them, diving phantoms, mobs coming for them or that hurt them), block arrows with a shield, and toss them food when they look hurt. Never attacks players, pets, villagers, golems or named mobs; neutral mobs only when they attack.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `player` | string |  |  | player to protect; defaults to the requesting player |
| `distance` | number (1..8) |  | `3` | follow distance, blocks |
| `range` | number (6..32) |  | `16` | protect this far around them |
| `feed` | boolean |  | `true` | toss food when their health is low (needs the server to send player health) |
| `keepFood` | integer (0..64) |  | `4` | food items to keep for itself |
| `chat` | boolean |  | `true` | short callouts in chat (fed you, ...) |
| `intercept` | boolean |  | `true` | meet a mob walking at the player 6-12 blocks out on its path instead of at the player |
| `pullAggro` | boolean |  | `true` | with two or more mobs on the player, hit each once and step off so they follow the bot |

### `feed_player`

Walk up to a player and toss them food from the inventory (the best food, 1-2 items), keeping some for itself.

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `player` | string |  |  | who to feed; defaults to the requesting player |
| `keepFood` | integer (0..64) |  | `4` | food items to keep for itself |

## combat

Fighting hostile mobs, guarding players and hunting animals for food.

### `attack`

Fight the most dangerous hostile mob nearby, or a specific entity by id. Never attacks players, villagers, golems, pets or named mobs.

| param | type | required | default | description |

| `entityId` | number |  |  | entity id; default the most dangerous hostile mob nearby |
| `radius` | number |  | `16` | how far to look for a target, in blocks |

### `guard`

Stay near a player and kill hostile mobs that come close to them, until stopped.

*long-running*

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `player` | string |  |  | player to protect; defaults to the requesting player |
| `radius` | number |  | `12` |  |

Fight back against the hostile mobs around, most dangerous first (used by reflexes).

Hunt passive animals (cow, pig, sheep, chicken, rabbit, mooshroom) for food and pick up the drops. Never touches pets, named, tamed or leashed animals, babies, villagers or players, and by default leaves fenced animals alone.

## construction

Building structures from blueprints.

### `build`

Build a whole structure from a blueprint. For "build a house" use small_house (cozy 5x5 wooden house: log corners, pitched stair roof, windows, door, torches, crafting table, chest, bed if there is wool). Others: cottage (bigger 7x7 house on a cobblestone foundation with porch, glass windows, furnace), cabin (log cabin), watchtower (ladder, fenced platform), fortress (15x15 walled compound to put a house in), hut (plain box, quick), shelter (emergency 3x3 box around the bot), wall_segment, platform, tower. Picks a flat, clear spot near whoever asked (never in protected areas or over player builds), fills small dips, digs bumps and plants, faces the door to the player (or an open side), places blocks with the right facing (stairs, slabs, logs, doors, torches...), checks every block afterwards and fixes mistakes, and skips blocks that are already right, so calling it again resumes an interrupted build. gather=true first gathers what is missing. Reports blocks built and what was skipped. Learned blueprints (captured, imported, designed) build the same way; blueprint_pick chooses one when the request names none.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |  | blueprint name: small_house (default house), cottage, cabin, watchtower, fortress, hut, shelter, wall_segment, platform, tower, or a learned one (blueprint_search finds them) |
| `x` | number |  |  | centre of the footprint; omit to pick a spot near the player |
| `y` | number |  |  | level of the floor (layer 0); default the ground there + 1 |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |
| `facing` | `north` \| `east` \| `south` \| `west` |  |  | side the entrance faces; default towards the player |
| `material` | string |  |  | main block, e.g. spruce_planks or cobblestone; default whatever fits that the bot has most of |
| `theme` | string |  |  | wood to build with: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark_oak, mangrove, cherry, pale_oak; default whatever wood the bot has most of |
| `gather` | boolean |  | `false` | gather missing materials first (chop trees, mine, craft) |
| `path` | boolean |  | `true` | dig a short dirt path from the door afterwards when the bot can make a shovel |
| `method` | `auto` \| `hand` \| `commands` |  |  | creative only: hand = place block by block like a player (default), commands = /fill and /setblock when the bot is op (fast; every command shows to other ops as an admin message), auto = the build.creativeMethod setting. Survival always builds by hand |
| `replace` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: also dig up and replace blocks in the footprint that look player-made (e.g. an older build of ours being upgraded). Only when the owner asked to fix, upgrade or rebuild something there |

### `build_plan`

What a blueprint needs vs what the bot carries, and where it would go. preview=true adds a text drawing (top view and every layer). Without a template, lists the blueprints.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string |  |  |  |
| `material` | string |  |  |  |
| `theme` | string |  |  | wood to build with: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark_oak, mangrove, cherry, pale_oak; default whatever wood the bot has most of |
| `x` | number |  |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |  |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |
| `facing` | `north` \| `east` \| `south` \| `west` |  |  |  |
| `preview` | boolean |  | `false` | include a text drawing of the structure |

## containers

Storing items in and taking them out of chests and barrels.

### `deposit`

Put items into the nearest chest/barrel (or the one at x y z). item="all" stores everything except tools, armour, food and anything in keep; `items` stores exactly those counts. Without x y z it never picks the pantry (settings.storage.chests role pantry) for anything but food.

*aliases: `store`*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | string |  | `"all"` | item name, or "all" |
| `count` | integer (..9007199254740991) |  |  | how many; default all of them |
| `keep` | array |  |  | item names never to store |
| `items` | object |  |  | exact items and counts to store, e.g. {"snowball": 16}; overrides item and count |
| `x` | number |  |  | container x; omit all three to use the nearest chest/barrel |
| `y` | number |  |  |  |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |

### `withdraw`

Take items out of the nearest chest/barrel (or the one at x y z).

*aliases: `take`*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | string | yes |  | item name, or "all" to empty the container |
| `count` | integer (..9007199254740991) |  |  | how many; default all of that item |
| `x` | number |  |  | container x; omit all three to use the nearest chest/barrel |
| `y` | number |  |  |  |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |

### `list_container`

Look inside its own chests (ones it placed) and the configured ones (settings.storage.chests) near home that it has not looked into lately, so what it remembers is right again: notes items taken or added, chests moved or broken, and says when the pantry runs low. Never opens anyone else's chest.

Remembers it as its own storage chest.

## food

Food self-sufficiency: scouting for animals and village farms, starting, tending and growing a farm of its own, gathering seeds, foraging berries, kelp and apples, breeding animals.

### `find_food`

Scout for food beyond what is in sight: first known food spots, then an expanding spiral around home (or here) out to `radius` blocks, by day, avoiding water, lava and protected areas, until it sees huntable animals or a village farm. Remembers what it finds as places (food:animals, food:village_farm, food:water). Does not hunt; use hunt or keep_fed after.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number (32..1024) |  | `200` | how far from home to scout, in blocks |
| `atNight` | boolean |  | `false` | also scout at night (dangerous) |
| `animals` | array |  | `["cow","pig","sheep","chicken","rabbit","mooshroom"]` | animals that count as food |
| `crops` | boolean |  | `true` | village farms (crops with villagers nearby) count as food too |
| `maxMinutes` | number (1..30) |  | `8` | give up after this long |
| `keepAtLeast` | integer (0..32) |  | `0` | only count animals above this many adults of a kind (a herd to spare) |
| `from` | `home` \| `here` |  | `"home"` | centre of the search: home (when set) or where the bot stands |
| `minRadius` | number (0..1024) |  | `0` | skip rings at or inside this radius (an earlier, smaller search covered them) |
| `seeds` | integer (0..64) |  | `0` | pick up this many seeds on the way by breaking grass next to the path (for a farm later) |

### `start_farm`

Start a small farm of its own: picks grass or dirt by water near home (or a place), outside protected areas and away from anybody's builds or fields (or pours water from a bucket), then gets seeds by breaking grass (or uses carrots, potatoes, beetroot seeds), makes a hoe if needed, tills a plot around the water, plants it, fences and lights it if it has the materials, and remembers it as farm:1, farm:2... for farm_loop/farm_setup. Needs digging enabled.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `place` | string |  |  | remembered place (or home) to farm near; default home, else here |
| `x` | number |  |  | farm near this x (with z) instead |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |
| `size` | integer (3..9) |  | `9` | plot side, odd, around one water block (9 = 80 farmland) |
| `radius` | number (8..96) |  | `48` | how far from the centre to look for water |
| `seeds` | integer (1..64) |  | `10` | seeds to collect before planting (breaks grass until it has them or gives up) |
| `fence` | boolean |  | `true` | fence the plot when it has (or can craft) enough fences |
| `light` | boolean |  | `true` | put torches on the corners when it has torches or coal |
| `spawnClearance` | number (0..256) |  | `48` | never farm within this distance of the world spawn |

### `tend_farm`

Look after its own farm (farm:1, farm:2...): put the water back if it is gone (with a bucket), plant bare farmland, till trampled dirt again and plant it, and grow the plot a ring at a time towards `size` around its water with the seeds it has, keeping `seedReserve` seeds for replanting; short of seeds it takes them from its own and configured chests near home first. Use harvest for ripe crops. Needs digging enabled for tilling.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `farm` | string |  |  | which farm (farm:1...); default the nearest |
| `size` | integer (3..9) |  | `9` | side of the square to grow the farm towards (one water block keeps 9x9 wet) |
| `seedReserve` | integer (0..32) |  | `4` | seeds kept for replanting: new cells only from seeds beyond these |
| `maxCells` | integer (1..80) |  | `40` | cells to plant or till at most this run |
| `fromChests` | boolean |  | `true` | short of seeds: take them from its own and configured chests near home first |
| `spawnClearance` | number (0..256) |  | `48` | never till within this distance of the world spawn |

### `gather_seeds`

Get seeds for a farm by breaking surface grass and ferns nearby (open to the sky and near its own height, never cave grass; wheat seeds drop about 1 in 8) and picking them up. Keeps going, patch by patch out to the radius, until it has the seeds, the time is up or the grass runs out. Skips protected areas and the world spawn. First takes wheat seeds from its own and configured chests near home (fromChests). Needs digging enabled for the grass.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | integer (1..64) |  | `10` | seeds to get |
| `fromChests` | boolean |  | `true` | take seeds from its own and configured chests near home before breaking grass |
| `radius` | number (4..128) |  | `32` | how far to look for grass |
| `maxMinutes` | number (0.5..10) |  | `3` | give up after this long |
| `spawnClearance` | number (0..256) |  | `48` | never break grass this close to the world spawn |

### `forage`

Stopgap food from what grows wild nearby: pick ripe sweet berries (the bush stays), cut kelp at the shore without diving (smelt it into dried kelp later), and with apples=true break oak and dark oak leaves for apples (about 1 in 200) and pick up apples lying around. Never on protected land.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | number (4..64) |  | `32` | how far to look |
| `max` | integer (1..32) |  | `8` | bushes or kelp stalks to take at most |
| `kinds` | array |  | `["berries","kelp"]` | what to forage |
| `apples` | boolean |  | `false` | also break leaves for apples (slow, low odds: a last resort) |
| `leaves` | integer (1..64) |  | `24` | leaves to break at most for apples |

### `breed`

Breed two adult animals of a kind it sees (cows/sheep with wheat, pigs with carrots/potatoes/beetroot, chickens with seeds), leading them towards its farm first when it has one nearby. Never feeds pets, named, leashed or fenced animals that are not on its own farm. Keeps seeds for replanting.

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `animal` | `cow` \| `mooshroom` \| `sheep` \| `pig` \| `chicken` \| `rabbit` |  |  | which kind; default the best one it has food for |
| `radius` | number (4..48) |  | `24` | how far to look for animals |
| `lure` | boolean |  | `true` | lead them to its farm first (when one is within 64 blocks) |
| `keepSeeds` | integer (0..64) |  | `8` | seeds to keep for replanting |
| `maxHerd` | integer (2..64) |  | `12` | do not breed a kind with this many adults around |

### `repair_farm`

Look at one of its own farms that site health marked bad (flooded, frozen) and repair it where it is when that is a small job: break the frozen water in the middle and keep it open, fill flooded field cells with dirt, put the water back with a bucket. A farm that reads fine again goes back on its list. When the repair is too big (settings farming.badFarm, repairMaxBlocks, repairTries) it leaves the farm for a new one elsewhere, or for the owners.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `farm` | string |  |  | which bad farm (farm:1...); default the nearest to home |
| `spawnClearance` | number (0..256) |  | `48` | never dig within this distance of the world spawn |

### `plot_farm`

Turn the farm plot its base keeps free inside the walls (base project farm_plot) into a farm, or extend its farm when the plot grew: water already in reach of the plot; on a plot of 5 and up a water bucket (carried, from a container, an empty one filled, or crafted from 3 iron) poured in the middle; ice it carries (only Silk Touch brings ice) broken in the middle; else a dry plot (crops on dry farmland still grow, about half as fast, as long as every tilled cell is planted). Short of seeds it takes them from its chests, then breaks grass near home. Torches give the crops light 9 and keep the middle water from freezing. Settings farming.plot, plotWater (auto | water | dry), plotSwap, plotSize, plotSeedRadius.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spawnClearance` | number (0..256) |  | `48` | never till within this distance of the world spawn |

### `fish`

Fish for food: takes a rod from its chests or makes one from 2 string and 3 sticks (taking what it lacks from its chests) when it has none, goes to open water near home (or breaks a hole in a frozen lake, which turns back into water over the lake), and fishes until it has `count` catches or `maxMinutes` pass. Cod and salmon are cooked later by keep_fed.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | integer (1..32) |  | `6` | catches to stop at |
| `maxMinutes` | number (1..30) |  | `5` | stop after this long |
| `radius` | number (8..96) |  | `48` | how far from home to look for water |

### `food_sources`

Say which food source it relies on for the long run (a farm, the base plot, a bad farm to repair, animals, fishing, foraging), in the order settings food.sources gives, and why each one before it was skipped.

No parameters.

## lighting

Spawn-proofing with torches.

### `light_up`

Spawn-proofs an area: finds the spots around a place (home, farm:1, coordinates, or here) where hostile mobs could spawn (block light below `target`; 1.21.1 monsters need light 0), works out the fewest torches that light them all, crafts torches from coal or charcoal (smelts charcoal from logs when out of coal) and places them: floor torches, wall torches where there is no floor; never on farmland, crops, paths, in front of doors, in water, near the world spawn or where the server refused a torch, and never breaking anything. Around its own farms it stays off the field and counts only the ground the field is on. Remembers its own torches. dry_run only reports.

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `place` | string |  |  | remembered place to light up, e.g. home or farm:1; default x/y/z or where it stands |
| `x` | number |  |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |  |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |
| `radius` | integer (2..48) |  | `16` | flat radius around the centre |
| `y_range` | integer (1..16) |  | `6` | blocks above and below the centre to look at |
| `target` | integer (1..15) |  | `8` | light every spawnable spot to at least this (1 stops spawns; higher leaves a margin) |
| `max_torches` | integer (1..64) |  | `16` | torches to place at most this time |
| `craft` | boolean |  | `true` | craft torches (and smelt charcoal) when it has too few |
| `spawn_clearance` | number (0..256) |  | `24` | never place within this distance of the world spawn |
| `surface` | boolean |  |  | only the ground connected to the centre's level, no caves under it; default on around its own farms |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | `false` | only report the dark spots and the planned torches |

## materials

Gathering and crafting everything a job needs.

### `gather_materials`

Get the materials for a job in one go: chops as many trees as needed (crafting a wooden axe first), turns logs into planks and sticks, crafts wooden items (stairs, slabs, fences, doors, trapdoors, ladders, crafting tables, chests, tools), mines cobblestone with a pickaxe and other simple blocks, makes the stone family (cobblestone/stone/stone brick slabs, stairs and walls, stone bricks, smooth stone; smelting cobblestone into stone in a furnace), and tries for the extras: torches (coal, or charcoal smelted from logs), glass panes (sand smelted into glass), a bed (wool from sheep nearby). Extras it can't get are skipped and reported. Give either items, e.g. {"planks": 80, "door": 1} ("planks", "log", "door", "stairs", "slab", "fence", "bed" mean any wood/colour), or template="small_house" for everything a blueprint needs. Prefer this over many chop_tree/craft calls. Needs digging enabled to chop or mine.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | object |  |  | item -> count, e.g. {"oak_planks": 64, "stick": 8, "door": 1} |
| `template` | string |  |  | blueprint name (see build_plan) to gather everything it needs |
| `material` | string |  |  | with template: the main block to use, e.g. spruce_planks or cobblestone |
| `theme` | string |  |  | wood to build with: oak, spruce, birch, dark_oak...; default whatever wood the bot has most of |
| `radius` | integer (8..64) |  | `32` | how far to look for trees and blocks |

## progression

Tool progression: stone, iron and diamond tools.

### `upgrade_tools`

Upgrade tools as far as possible right now: wooden pickaxe -> stone tools (mines the cobblestone) -> furnace from 8 cobblestone -> smelt iron (coal, or charcoal made from logs) -> iron tools -> diamond tools if it has diamonds. Covers pickaxe, sword, axe and shovel, armour optionally. Stops at the best tier it can reach and says what is missing (e.g. no iron ore seen). Safe mining: without a weapon, food (and a shield or armour if mining.gear asks) it only takes ore near the surface and says "not ready to mine: ..." instead of going into caves. In creative it just takes the tools.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `up_to` | `stone` \| `iron` \| `diamond` |  | `"iron"` | highest tier to aim for |
| `armour` | boolean |  | `false` | also make iron armour (chestplate, leggings, helmet, boots) after the iron pickaxe |
| `bucket` | boolean |  | `false` | also make a bucket right after the iron pickaxe |
| `shield` | boolean |  | `false` | also make a shield (1 iron ingot, 6 planks) after the bucket |
| `kinds` | array |  |  | tool kinds to upgrade; default pickaxe, sword, axe, shovel |
| `prospect` | boolean |  | `true` | when no iron ore is in sight, dig a staircase and strip mine to look for some |
| `safe` | boolean |  | `true` | safe mining (settings.mining): only go deeper than mining.safeDepth with a weapon, food and the gear it asks for; avoid caves, light tunnels, climb out when losing underground |

### `dig_mine`

Go mining in its own staircase mine near home: a 1-wide, 2-high staircase at 45 degrees from a dry, unprotected spot near home (never straight down, never next to lava or water, never into a cave) down to settings.mine.depthY (16: iron depth), then a main tunnel with side branches, mining the iron, coal, copper (and diamonds with an iron pickaxe) it sees in the walls, torches on the way, and back up the stairs when it has what it came for, the time is up, the inventory is full, food or the pickaxe run out, or it gets hurt. The mine is remembered: the next trip carries on where this one stopped.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ore` | `iron` \| `coal` \| `copper` \| `diamond` \| `gold` \| `redstone` \| `lapis` |  | `"iron"` | what it goes for (it stops once it has `count` of it) |
| `count` | integer (0..256) |  | `0` | how many of that ore to bring (raw iron, coal...); 0 = until the time, inventory or tools run out |
| `max_minutes` | number (1..60) |  |  | time down there at most (default settings.mine.minutes, 15) |
| `fresh` | boolean |  | `false` | start a new mine even when it knows one |

## roads

Roads and staircases between buildings: planning, building, removing.

### `build_road`

Plan and build a road with proper stairs between two places, like a person would: straight flights, stairs only on straight stretches (every stair facing up), flat landings at turns, switchbacks on steep slopes, a base filled down to the ground, head-room cut, wall railings where the drop beside it is 2 or more, never through buildings, trees or protected areas, joining existing roads at T-junctions. From the bot (or from_x/from_z, or `from` = a saved place or player) to x y z (or `to`). A point next to a door starts or ends straight out of that door. dry_run=true only plans and lists the materials. redo (a road id from road_list) builds a removed road again. Survival gathers stone bricks first; creative builds by hand or with commands.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number |  |  | target x |
| `y` | number |  |  | target walking height (default the ground there + 1) |
| `z` | number |  |  | target z |
| `to` | string |  |  | target: a saved place name, a player name, or "me" |

| `from_y` | number |  |  |  |
| `from_z` | number |  |  |  |
| `from` | string |  |  | start: a saved place, a player, or "me" (default where the bot stands) |
| `redo` | integer (-9007199254740991..9007199254740991) |  |  | id of a road built earlier (see road_list): build it again on the same line |
| `width` | integer (1..5) |  |  | lanes (1, 3 or 5; even widths round up); default the road.width setting (3) |
| `palette` | `stone_bricks` \| `cobblestone` \| `stone` \| `oak` \| `spruce` |  |  | look: stone_bricks, cobblestone, stone, oak, spruce; default the road.palette setting (stone_bricks: stone brick floor and stairs, cobblestone base, stone brick wall railings) |
| `lanterns` | boolean |  |  | lanterns on posts at the landings (default the road.lanterns setting) |
| `bridge` | boolean |  | `false` | may cross water or lava on a deck |

| `method` | `auto` \| `hand` \| `commands` |  |  | creative only: hand (default, block by block) or commands (/fill and /setblock when op; every command shows to other ops) |

Join buildings with roads and stairs, cheapest roads first, each door getting a straight start, later roads joining earlier ones at T-junctions. Buildings come from: what the bot built (source=built, the default), doors among its own blocks (own), doors within radius of here (nearby), or door coordinates (doors="x y z; x y z"). ## search

Finding things (find_target) and fetching them for players (bring_item, fetch_drops) without an LLM.

### `find_target`

Find something and report where it is: blocks and families (iron, diamonds, coal, logs, sand, water, lava), mobs (sheep, cows, villager), structures (village, nether portal, chest), biomes (desert, snow, ocean) or modded names. Looks at what is loaded around it, then remembered spots, then scouts a spiral on the surface by day (and can strip mine for ores). Remembers the spot as a place (found:iron for iron), reports coordinates, distance and direction from you, and comes back (or stays there with go). With bring it also fetches count of it and hands them over.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | yes |  | what to look for, e.g. iron, sheep, water, village, desert |
| `radius` | number (16..512) |  | `160` | how far to search, in blocks |
| `max_minutes` | number (1..30) |  | `8` | give up after this long |
| `bring` | boolean |  | `false` | also fetch some of it (blocks and items only) and hand it over |
| `count` | integer (1..256) |  | `1` | how many to bring |
| `go` | boolean |  | `false` | walk there and stay, instead of coming back to report |
| `prospect` | boolean |  | `false` | ores: strip mine for it when none is in sight (always on with bring) |
| `at_night` | boolean |  | `false` | also scout at night (dangerous) |
| `exposed` | boolean |  | `false` | ores: only count ore with an open face (a cliff, a shallow cave) within mining.safeDepth of the surface, not ore buried in rock or deep in a cave |

### `bring_item`

Bring a player some of an item: from the inventory, from my own chests (ones I placed or listed in settings.storage.chests, never anyone else's), by crafting it (simple recipes), by gathering it (chop, mine, harvest village or own farms), or by finding its source first. Then walks to the player, follows them if they move, tosses it to them and says how many they really got.

*long-running*

Go to where a player (default: whoever asked) died and bring their dropped items back, if the bot can get there before they despawn (5 minutes). Uses the death message and where it last saw them, or coordinates you give.

## woodcutting

Felling trees.

### `chop_tree`

Fell the nearest natural tree (any wood type): cut the logs, climbing the trunk on a pillar for the ones out of reach from the ground (and taking the pillar down again), pick up the drops and plant a sapling. With rings it widens the search (remembered tree spots, then ring by ring, with a trip out and back) instead of giving up. Crafts a wooden axe first if there is none and the inventory has the wood. Needs digging enabled. For "get N planks/logs" or materials for a build, prefer gather_materials, which chops as many trees as needed.

*aliases: `chop`*

### `we_outline`

Cover all six faces of the selected region (//faces, also known as //outline): walls, floor and ceiling. Owners only; block limit and protected areas apply.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | string | yes |  | block or WorldEdit pattern, e.g. stone_bricks, oak_planks, 50%stone,50%cobblestone, oak_stairs[facing=north] |
| `protected_ok` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: allow it inside a protected area or the spawn area, when the owner explicitly asked for that spot |

### `we_hollow`

Hollow out the objects in the selected region (//hollow), leaving a shell of the given thickness, inside filled with the pattern (default air). Owners only; block limit and protected areas apply.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `thickness` | integer (1..8) |  | `1` |  |
| `pattern` | string |  | `"air"` | what to fill the inside with |
| `protected_ok` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: allow it inside a protected area or the spawn area, when the owner explicitly asked for that spot |

### `we_copy`

Copy the selected region to the WorldEdit clipboard (//copy). The clipboard remembers where I stood: we_paste puts it back relative to where I stand then. Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

No parameters.

### `we_cut`

Cut the selected region to the WorldEdit clipboard (//cut): copies it and leaves air. Owners only; block limit and protected areas apply.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protected_ok` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: allow it inside a protected area or the spawn area, when the owner explicitly asked for that spot |

### `we_paste`

Paste the WorldEdit clipboard (//paste) where I stand, or walk to x y z first. skip_air=true (-a) leaves existing blocks where the clipboard has air. Owners only; the clipboard size is checked against the block limit and protected areas first.

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skip_air` | boolean |  | `true` | -a: don't paste air |
| `original` | boolean |  | `false` | -o: paste where it was copied from, not where I stand |
| `x` | number |  |  | walk here first (where I stand is where the clipboard origin goes) |
| `y` | number |  |  |  |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |
| `protected_ok` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: allow it inside a protected area or the spawn area, when the owner explicitly asked for that spot |

### `we_rotate`

Rotate the WorldEdit clipboard around the vertical axis (//rotate), in steps of 90 degrees. Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `degrees` | any | yes |  | 90, 180, 270 or -90 |

### `we_flip`

Flip (mirror) the WorldEdit clipboard (//flip) along a direction; default the way I face. Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `north` \| `south` \| `east` \| `west` \| `up` \| `down` |  |  |  |

### `we_undo`

Undo my last WorldEdit change(s) (//undo). Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `times` | integer (1..10) |  | `1` |  |

### `we_redo`

Redo WorldEdit changes I undid (//redo). Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `times` | integer (1..10) |  | `1` |  |

### `we_schem_list`

List the schematics in the server's WorldEdit schematics folder (//schem list). Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

No parameters.

### `we_schem_load`

Load a schematic from the server's WorldEdit schematics folder into the clipboard (//schem load name), then we_paste puts it down. Only files already on the server; I can't upload any. Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | schematic name, with or without .schem |

### `we_schem_save`

Save the WorldEdit clipboard as a schematic in the server's schematics folder (//schem save name). Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | schematic name (letters, digits, _ and -) |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | `false` | -f: replace a schematic of that name |

### `we_raw`

Run one other WorldEdit command from a whitelist (size, count, distr, sel, desel, pos1, pos2, hpos1, hpos2, expand, contract, shift, outset, inset, chunk, clearclipboard, set, replace, walls, faces, outline, hollow, overlay, naturalize, smooth, center, centre, line, move, stack), e.g. "//expand 5 up" or "//stack 3 north". Commands that change blocks need a selection from we_select and stay under the block limit. Owners only.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | string | yes |  | the command with its arguments, e.g. "//expand 5 up" |
| `protected_ok` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: allow it inside a protected area or the spawn area, when the owner explicitly asked for that spot |

### `we_build`

Build a library blueprint with WorldEdit when an owner asks for it: if WorldEdit is available and the server already has a schematic with that name (//schem list), load and paste it (-a) at x y z (or where I stand); otherwise, or when that fails, build it the normal way (build). I can't upload schematics to the server. Owners only.

*long-running*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `template` | string | yes |  | blueprint name (also the schematic name looked for on the server) |
| `schematic` | string |  |  | schematic name on the server if it differs from the blueprint name |
| `x` | number |  |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |  |
| `z` | number |  |  |  |
| `facing` | `north` \| `east` \| `south` \| `west` |  |  | for the normal build fallback |
| `fallback` | boolean |  | `true` | build it normally when WorldEdit can't |
| `gather` | boolean |  | `false` | normal build: gather missing materials first |
| `protected_ok` | boolean |  | `false` | owners only: allow it inside a protected area or the spawn area, when the owner explicitly asked for that spot |

## behaviors (brain)

Registered by `behaviorsBrain()`, see [Behaviours](../guide/behaviors.md).

### `behavior_list`

List the behaviours this bot can arm: armed behaviours keep running on their own between your turns (keep_fed finds and eats food, stay_safe backs off at low health, follow_owner, guard_area, farm_loop...). Pass a name for its options and defaults.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |  | one behaviour to explain in detail |

### `behavior_status`

Show which behaviours are armed, their options, what is running now, last outcomes and cooldowns.

*non-exclusive*

No parameters.

### `behavior_arm`

Arm a behaviour so it keeps running on its own, without further turns, until disarmed (it survives restarts). Arm keep_fed so you look after your own food, stay_safe to back off at low health, follow_owner or guard_owner to stay with your owner, guard_area to defend a spot, farm_loop / chop_wood_loop for ongoing chores. Prefer this over doing an ongoing job turn by turn.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | behaviour name from behavior_list, e.g. keep_fed |
| `options` | any |  |  | options as an object, e.g. {"below": 10}; in chat as key=value pairs, e.g. below=10 animals=cow,pig |

### `behavior_disarm`

Switch an armed behaviour off (stops it now if it is running). It stays off across restarts.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | behaviour name from behavior_list, e.g. keep_fed |

### `behavior_configure`

Change the options of a behaviour (armed or not) without arming or disarming it, e.g. keep_fed below=10.

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  | behaviour name from behavior_list, e.g. keep_fed |
| `options` | any |  |  | options as an object, e.g. {"below": 10}; in chat as key=value pairs, e.g. below=10 animals=cow,pig |

### `behavior_reset`

Forget runtime arm/disarm/configure changes and go back to the profile's behaviours (one, or all without a name).

*non-exclusive*

| param | type | required | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |  | behaviour to reset; default all |
